newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-IWS sees slow Australian wool prices recovery.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-IWS sees slow Australian wool prices recovery.

text.p: The International Wool Secretariat (IWS) said Australian market growth was expected to be maintained at current levels with prices slowly recovering to between 600 cents and 650 cents a kg clean.
"We've got a slow price recovery on our hands. We're probably not far off the 600 to 650 cents a kg region," IWS director of information and planning, Ian Hilton told a news conference on Tuesday.
Presenting the latest IWS wool business conditions survey for the September quarter, Hilton said the price outlook for wool was consistent with other forecasters.
The eastern market wool indicator last week rose by 11 cents to 575 cents a kg clean, while the western market wool indicator rose 10 cents to 535 cents a kg.
Hilton said he was still cautious about forecasting the long-term price trend for wool.
"Hopefully 1997 will offer better opportunities for price improvement," he said. "While order levels have improved in the major markets, the mood is still cautious."
The IWS survey showed order levels in the major wool textile markets had improved but regional results were still mixed and business was price sensitive world-wide, Hilton said.
These conditions came at a time when Australia's supply of wool so far this season had increased by about 34 percent compared with this time last year, he said.
The survey showed markets for Australian wool in the United States and the United Kingdon continued to grow while there was a cautious pipeline recovery in Japan, Hilton said.
"Western Europe is buying but it is still hand to mouth," he said.
China was returning to traditional suppliers and orders were expcted to improve in the next quarter, he said.
"High fabric stocks combined with weaker fabric orders in the December quarter could cause some slowdown of business conditions at earlier stages in the new year," Hilton said.
The survey reported a cautious recovery in the wool textile industries in Japan, Korea and Taiwan.
He said early stage processing in Australia continued to grow in the September quarter but at a more moderate rate.
"Australian early stage processors remain largely neutral in their outlook for the December quarter, expecting growth to be maintained at current levels and orders to remain unchanged," Hilton said.

David Connors, IWS group manager, international marketing, said the IWS would continue efforts to rejuvenate the Woolmark brand which was becoming misunderstood by international markets, including Australia.
The IWS planned to use extensions or sub-brands of the Woolmark label to promote Merino and Merino extra-fine labels, Conners said.
The Woolmark brand, now licensed for use by about 80 percent of all users of wool, returned A$18 million in licence fees in 1995/96, Conners said.
The IWS is a global organisation representing wool growers in Australia, South Africa and Uruguay.
-- Sydney Newsroom 6-1 9373-1800
